## Key FeaturesSVG Image

- The State Street® SPDR® S&P® Biotech ETF seeks to provide investment results that, before fees and expenses, correspond generally to the total return performance of the S&P® Biotechnology Select Industry™ Index (the "Index")
- Seeks to provide exposure to the Biotechnology segment of the S&P TMI, which comprises the following sub-industries: Biotechnology
- Seeks to track a modified equal weighted index which provides the potential for unconcentrated industry exposure across large, mid and small cap stocks
- Allows investors to take strategic or tactical positions at a more targeted level than traditional sector based investing

## About this BenchmarkSVG Image

The S&P Biotechnology Select Industry® represents the biotechnology segment of the S&P Total Market Index (“S&P TMI”). The S&P TMI is designed to track the broad U.S. equity market. The biotechnology segment of the S&P TMI comprises the Biotechnology sub-industry. The Index is modified equal weighted.

## Purchase InformationSVG Image

**Buying and Selling ETFs**

ETFs are flexible and easy to trade. Investors buy and sell them like stocks, typically through a brokerage account. Investors can also employ traditional stock trading techniques; including stop orders, limit orders, margin purchases, and short sales using ETFs. They are listed on major US Stock Exchanges.

ETFs are subject to risk similar to those of stocks including those regarding short-selling and margin account maintenance.

Ordinary brokerage commissions apply.

In general, ETFs can be expected to move up or down in value with the value of the applicable index. Although ETF shares may be bought and sold on the exchange through any brokerage account, ETF shares are not individually redeemable from the Fund. Investors may acquire ETFs and tender them for redemption through the Fund in Creation Unit Aggregations only. Please see the prospectus for more details.

Unless otherwise noted all information contained herein is that of the State Street® SPDR® S&P® Biotech ETF.

Holdings and sectors shown are as of the date indicated and are subject to change. This information should not be considered a recommendation to invest in a particular sector or to buy or sell any security shown. It is not known whether the sectors or securities shown will be profitable in the future.

As with all stocks, you may be required to deposit more money or securities into your margin account if the equity, including the amount attributable to your ETF shares, declines.

The S&P Select Industry series is designed to measure the performance of narrow GICS (Global Industry Classification Standard) sub-industries. The S&P Biotech Select Industry Index is an equal-weighted index that draws constituents from the Biotechnology segment of the S&P TMI. Liquidity and market capitalization screens are applied to the index to ensure investability.

sources.title: XBI June 30 2026 factsheet
sources.excerpt: The Index is modified equal weighted. Gross Expense Ratio 0.35; Net Expense Ratio 0.35. Passively managed funds invest by sampling the index, holding a range of securities that, in the aggregate, approximates the full Index in terms of key risk factors and other characteristics. This may cause the fund to experience tracking errors relative to performance of the index. Liquidity and market capitalization screens are applied to the index to ensure investability. Because of their narrow focus, sector funds tend to be more volatile than broadly diversified funds. Certain State Street affiliates provide services and receive fees from the SPDR ETFs.

price.note: Regular-session close, not NAV or after-hours. Observed current fund-unit basis; no ADR conversion.

shares.note: Sponsor millions normalized to units; rounded to 0.01 million. Oct8 units are not verified Oct9 units.

market_cap.note: ETF net assets/AUM are net portfolio value, not reported corporate equity market capitalization. No comparable dated reported quoted-unit capitalization retained; native price times units remains only an arithmetic product.

revenue.note: Investment income and portfolio turnover are not corporate customer revenue; fund mandate is index exposure.

net_income.note: Fund net investment income and realized/unrealized gains are investment-company results, not consolidated operating-company GAAP net income.

operating_cash_flow.note: Creations/redemptions and portfolio security cash flows do not measure operating-company cash generation.

capital_expenditure.note: Fund portfolio purchases are investments, not cash PP&E capital spending; no operating-company capex applies.

cash.note: Any fund cash/collateral is a portfolio allocation/settlement item, not consolidated corporate liquidity available for capital allocation.

debt.note: Underlying bond holdings (especially TLT Treasuries) are fund assets, not the fund operating-company debt; settlement liabilities are not a comparable corporate capital structure.

eps.note: No corporate GAAP diluted EPS earning-capacity anchor for an index fund; distributions and NAV changes are not operating EPS.

fund_nav.note: Sponsor net asset value per fund unit; not executable market price.

fund_net_assets.note: Sponsor AUM/net assets. State Street observed millions normalized by 1,000,000.

expense_ratio.note: Annual expense ratio fraction; observed sponsor 0.35% divided by 100. Annual fund cost, not corporate operating margin.

prior_close.note: Both publisher pages show Oct8 close; intentionally separate from latest Oct9 quote, not false same-period corroboration.

sec_yield.note: 30-day SEC annualized yield after fund expenses; fraction not percentage points.

distribution_yield.note: Sum of distributions in past365 days divided by NAV; not a forward promise.

model_applicability: Corporate EPS model intentionally omitted: fund NAV and underlying equity/bond exposure require fund-specific analysis.
